memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Curtains fifteen cubits long were on one side of the entrance, with three posts and three bases, and curtains fifteen cubits long were on the other side of the entrance to the courtyard, with three posts and three bases." - Exod 38:14-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Do the arithmetic. The east side was fifty cubits wide. Fifteen cubits of curtain on one side, fifteen on the other — leaving a gap of twenty cubits.

Twenty cubits is around nine metres. The entrance was nearly twice as wide as either curtain beside it.

God did not build a narrow crack for people to squeeze through. The way into His courtyard was the widest single feature of that wall.

Hold two truths together here. There was only one entrance — you could not come in from the north or west, and Scripture is clear that there is one way to the Father (John 14:6). But that one entrance was wide.

Some people imagine God as reluctant, admitting only a select few after careful scrutiny. This chapter says otherwise. One door, generously wide, facing the sunrise, with nothing blocking it.

Jesus said, "Whoever comes to me I will never drive away" (John 6:37). And the Bible closes with an invitation: whoever is thirsty, let them come; let whoever wishes take the free gift of the water of life (Rev 22:17).

If you have wondered whether there is room for you — look at the measurements. There is room.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you picture God as reluctant or welcoming?
2. Have you assumed you are somehow outside the invitation?
3. Who could you tell this week that the door is wide?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that the way in is wide and the invitation is real. Help me walk in and bring others with me. Amen.
